Hey folks! I've read previous threads about making skill limits, but they seem geared towards receiving skills from like Skill Vendors or Skill Point systems. posts.author: Eliaquim
posts.body:
Hi there!
Made a little mockup with events. Well, almost like a plugin in a common event... haha
1 - First you iterate through all party members and check if any of them has more than 4 skills (It says "> 3 " because arrays in javascript always start with the index 0. Meaning 0 is also a skill).
We flip a switch so we can use that as a condition to show the choice so the player can select what skill to forget.
If does, we store the Actor Name and id on variables.
then store all skill names on variables (to be used on choice commands)
then store all the skill ids to be used on later script calls.
2 - We make each choice with each skill the actor already have.
And for each choice, we use the script call so the actor can forget the skill related to the choice.
Then on the end of the choice event, turn off the Switch 270.
This is a basic structure, without plugins. I guess you can start with this if you want.
You can place this on a parallel event to run through all the game. Put a wait 10 frames on the end of the event so you don't need to worry about performance.
That will not only cover the cases when level up, but also if you want to teach a skill to an actor with event commands for example.
Hope it helps!
Script call text:
JavaScript:
for(const member of $gameParty.members()){
const skills = member.skills()
 if(skills.lenght > 3){
  $gameSwitches.setValue(270, true)
  $gameVariables.setValue(268, member.name())
  $gameVariables.setValue(269, member.actorId())

  $gameVariables.setValue(270, skills[0].name)
  $gameVariables.setValue(271, skills[1].name)
  $gameVariables.setValue(272, skills[2].name)
  $gameVariables.setValue(273, skills[3].name)
  $gameVariables.setValue(274, skills[4].name)

  $gameVariables.setValue(275, skills[0].id)
  $gameVariables.setValue(276, skills[1].id)
  $gameVariables.setValue(277, skills[2].id)
  $gameVariables.setValue(278, skills[3].id)
  $gameVariables.setValue(279, skills[4].id)
  // Necessary add a break here, in case more than one actor has more than 4 skill at the same time. 
  // With this we can deal with one at the time.
  break

 }
}

It will check the others because it's a parallel event. When the break is used, the loop will stop with the variables assigned.
Then it will proceed to what left of the event list.
When the event ends, since it is a parallel event, it will run again, checking the party members all over again.

        $gameVariables.setValue(277, skills[2].id)
        $gameVariables.setValue(278, skills[3].id)
        $gameVariables.setValue(279, skills[4].id)
        break
    }

}

There are two problems here.
1 - You are using the same switch that activates the common parallel event to also checks when the actor has gained more than 4 skills on the conditional branch. They need to be different switches. One for activate the event. Another one to be set to true inside the script call and on the conditional branch.
2 - You have a plugin called SkillCheck that is calling the same common event. So that is why the common event is being called twice.
once I deactivate that plugin and fixed the switches, everything worked just fine.
